name: Sleep-EDF Database Expanded
subjects: 100 (78 Sleep Cassette IDs parsed from RECORDS, plus 22 Sleep Telemetry subjects stated on the project page)
recordings: 197 whole-night PSGs (153 cassette, 44 telemetry)
modalities: EEG (Fpz-Cz, Pz-Oz), horizontal EOG, chin EMG, event marker; cassette recordings often also include oro-nasal respiration and rectal temperature
sampling_rate: EEG and EOG 100 Hz. Telemetry EMG 100 Hz. Cassette chin EMG is a 1 Hz envelope; cassette airflow, temperature, and event marker are 1 Hz
annotations: Manual Rechtschaffen and Kales hypnogram: W, R, 1, 2, 3, 4, movement, unscored. Technician identity is encoded in the hypnogram filename; one hypnogram per recording
clinical_text: No
license: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
research_use: Open download. Attribution required. The license permits reuse, including commercial use, under ODC-By 1.0
paper: Kemp et al., IEEE TBME 2000;47:1185-1194; Mourtazaev et al., Sleep 1995;18:557-564
doi: Unknown as a dedicated dataset DOI on the checked page
multi_expert: No parallel labels per epoch. Filename marks which technician scored each recording
timed_events: Hypnogram epochs. No spindle, K-complex, arousal, or apnea event layer is described
cover_stage2: Strong external benchmark for EEG staging and domain shift. Weak for expert disagreement and event-level pointers
notes: The 2002 Sleep-EDF release is an earlier subset, not an independent cohort. Cassette and telemetry differ in EMG sampling and in medication exposure: telemetry is a temazepam versus placebo study in people with mild sleep-onset difficulty.

name: CAP Sleep Database
subjects: 108 recordings: 16 healthy subjects and 92 pathological recordings. The page does not separately prove that every pathological file is a distinct person
recordings: 108 PSGs (16 controls, 40 NFLE, 22 RBD, 10 PLM, 9 insomnia, 5 narcolepsy, 4 SDB, 2 bruxism)
modalities: At least 3 EEG channels, 2 EOG, submental EMG, bilateral anterior tibial EMG, airflow, thoracic and abdominal effort, SaO2, ECG; some bipolar EEG
sampling_rate: Not a single rate on the project page. Header of n1.edf on 2026-11-05: EEG and EOG 512 Hz; the first EMG channel read was 256 Hz. Other records were not scanned
annotations: R&K sleep stages plus CAP phase A events with onset, duration, and a location field naming the signal or signals where the event was observed. Body position is present for some subjects
clinical_text: No narrative report. Event rows include a location string
license: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
research_use: Open download. Attribution required under ODC-By 1.0
paper: Terzano et al., Sleep Medicine 2001;2:537-553 (CAP atlas). Database contributed by Terzano, Parrino, and colleagues
doi: Unknown as a dedicated dataset DOI on the checked page
multi_expert: No. Scoring is attributed to the Parma sleep-center team, not to independent parallel labels
timed_events: Yes. CAP A phases have start time, duration, and channel location. This is event annotation, not a claim-to-evidence link
cover_stage2: Best open source of channel-named, timed EEG microstructure. Useful for building pointers; it does not supervise pointer-grounded diagnostic claims
notes: Pathology counts are recording groups published on the PhysioNet page. Sampling is header-specific and should not be assumed identical for every file.

name: Haaglanden Medisch Centrum sleep staging database
subjects: 151 recordings; reported sex counts are 85 male and 66 female
recordings: 151 whole-night PSGs in version 1.1
modalities: EEG F4-M1, C4-M1, O2-M1, C3-M2; EOG E1-M2 and E2-M2; bipolar chin EMG; one ECG lead
sampling_rate: 256 Hz for all listed signals
annotations: Manual AASM v2.4 hypnogram and lights-off/on markers. Files are clipped to the scored interval
clinical_text: No
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
research_use: Open download. Attribution required. CC BY 4.0 permits adaptation and commercial use
paper: Alvarez-Estevez and Rijsman, PLoS ONE 2021;16:e0256111
multi_expert: No
timed_events: Lights-off/on and stage epochs only. Respiratory, arousal, and limb events are not the released annotation layer
cover_stage2: Best medium-size heterogeneous clinical staging set for cross-dataset tests. Not an inter-rater or event-pointer set
notes: Version 1.1 removed SN014, SN064, and SN135 because of unfixable signal errors. Do not mix version 1.0 and 1.1 counts. In-hospital and ambulatory recordings are pooled. Dataset DOI is the PhysioNet citation; the paper DOI is 10.1371/journal.pone.0256111.

name: PSG-IPA
subjects: 20 PSG recordings. A separate unique-patient count is not stated
recordings: 20 PSGs: 5 assigned to each of staging, EEG arousals, leg movements, and respiratory events
modalities: EEG F4-M1, C4-M1 or Cz-M1, O2-M1; two EOG; chin and bilateral tibial EMG; ECG; nasal pressure; thoracic and abdominal effort; SpO2
sampling_rate: EEG, EOG, chin EMG, ECG, and nasal pressure 256 Hz; tibial EMG 128-256 Hz; effort belts 32 Hz; SpO2 4 Hz
annotations: Twelve technologists each scored manual and computer-assisted versions of their assigned task. Staging files contain stage labels. Event tasks contain onset and offset edits. Event tasks were given a prefilled hypnogram that scorers could not change
clinical_text: No
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
research_use: Open download. Attribution required
paper: Alvarez-Estevez and Rijsman, PLoS ONE 2022;17:e0275530
multi_expert: Yes. Twelve scorers, two settings. Independent staging labels exist for 5 recordings, not for all 20
timed_events: Yes for arousals, leg movements, and respiratory events, with human edits of onset and offset
claim_evidence_labels: No prebuilt claim-source-pointer triples. Event boundaries can be used to construct pointers
cover_stage2: Highest-priority open set for expert disagreement and boundary uncertainty. Too small to train a stager
notes: Selected in 2019 from HMC clinical PSGs to balance scoring difficulty. Computer-assisted files start from an automatic first pass. Do not treat the prefilled hypnogram on event tasks as a second independent staging.

name: MIT-BIH Polysomnographic Database
subjects: 16 male subjects in the current project text (ages 32-56, drawn from 60). RECORDS lists 18 waveform files because some subjects are split
recordings: 18 waveform files; durations 2-7 hours, not all whole nights
modalities: ECG, EEG, EOG, chin EMG, invasive blood pressure, SpO2, nasal and chest respiration, and cardiac volume on the original selection. Not every file contains every signal
sampling_rate: 250 Hz, 12-bit, as stated for the digitized recordings
annotations: Reviewed QRS annotations and R&K sleep stages. Original distribution also described apnea and CPAP timing
clinical_text: No
license: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
research_use: Open download. Attribution required
paper: Ichimaru and Moody, Psychiatry and Clinical Neurosciences 1999;53:175-177
multi_expert: No
timed_events: QRS annotations are explicit. Apnea and CPAP timing are described in the project text; confirm the annotation files before use
cover_stage2: Useful historical multimodal apnea physiology set. Too small and too old as a modern staging benchmark
notes: The current abstract says 16 subjects, while the file index contains 18 records (slp01a/b, slp02a/b, and slp67x among them). Keep those counts separate.

name: St. Vincent's University Hospital / University College Dublin Sleep Apnea Database
subjects: 25 adults (21 male, 4 female; age 50 ± 10 years)
recordings: 25 full overnight PSGs plus simultaneous three-channel Holter ECG
modalities: Two EEG, two EOG, submental EMG, ECG, oro-nasal airflow, ribcage and abdomen movement, SpO2, snoring, body position; separate Holter ECG
sampling_rate: From the EDF header of ucddb002.rec on 2026-11-05: EEG 128 Hz, EOG and EMG 64 Hz, ECG 128 Hz, airflow, effort, SpO2, and sound 8 Hz. Other records were not scanned
annotations: One technologist scored R&K stages, including artifact and indeterminate, and timed obstructive, central, and mixed apneas, hypopneas, and periodic breathing
clinical_text: No narrative report. A subject spreadsheet contains demographics and AHI
license: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
research_use: Open download. Attribution required
paper: Database description on PhysioNet. Collection led at St Vincent's University Hospital and University College Dublin
multi_expert: No
timed_events: Yes. Respiratory events have time of occurrence and type. Stages are in a separate epoch file
cover_stage2: Small but clean open set for aligning respiratory-event intervals with stage epochs, including artifact and indeterminate labels
notes: Suspected sleep-disordered breathing; AHI 24.1 ± 20.3. Recording dates were removed. DOI taken from the PhysioNet discovery field on the project page.

name: Apnea-ECG Database
subjects: Not stated. Seventy records are not seventy proven subjects: c05 and c06 come from the same original recording
recordings: 70 ECG records (35 learning, 35 test), about 7-10 hours each. Eight records also include respiration and SpO2
modalities: Continuous ECG for all records. Resp C, Resp A, Resp N, and SpO2 for a01-a04, b01, and c01-c03 only
sampling_rate: ECG 100 Hz. Additional-signal rates are in the per-record headers and were not re-read here
annotations: Expert minute-by-minute apnea presence for the 35 learning records, based on simultaneously recorded respiration that is not included for most records. Machine QRS marks are unaudited. No sleep stages
clinical_text: No
license: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
research_use: Open download. Attribution required. Learning-set apnea labels are the supervised subset
paper: Penzel, Moody, Mark, Goldberger, and Peter, Computers in Cardiology 2000;27:255-258
doi: Unknown as a dedicated dataset DOI on the checked page
multi_expert: No
timed_events: Minute apnea labels, not sample-level event intervals and not sleep stages
cover_stage2: Not a sleep-staging or EEG evidence set. Keep it in apnea-from-ECG work only
notes: Test-set apnea annotations are not in the released annotation files described on the page. Do not describe this as a full PSG cohort.

name: You Snooze You Win: PhysioNet/Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2018
subjects: 1,985 subjects monitored at the MGH sleep laboratory
recordings: 1,985 PSGs partitioned into training 994 and test 989
modalities: Six EEG (F3-M2, F4-M1, C3-M2, C4-M1, O1-M2, O2-M1), left EOG, chin/chest/abdomen EMG, ECG, airflow and respiratory effort as provided in the records, SaO2
sampling_rate: 200 Hz; SaO2 was resampled to 200 Hz
annotations: Training set: AASM stages in non-overlapping 30 s epochs (wake, N1, N2, N3, REM, undefined) and sample-level arousals, including respiratory events. This pass did not confirm that reference labels ship with the test partition
clinical_text: No report corpus. Summary clinical tables are in the project description
license: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
research_use: Open download without credentialing. Attribution required
paper: Ghassemi et al., You Snooze, You Win, Computing in Cardiology 2018
multi_expert: No. Stages were annotated by MGH clinical staff; parallel independent copies are not described
timed_events: Yes in training: target and non-target arousal regions and respiratory event classes have sample-level locations
cover_stage2: Largest open clinical PSG with timed arousals. Use it to build event pointers and proxy-difficult epochs, not as multi-rater supervision
notes: The 1.0.0 page also displays a newer latest DOI, 10.13026/1q9b-ge17. This entry was checked against version 1.0.0 only. Confirm whether a later version adds test labels before using the test partition as labeled data.

name: Motion and heart rate from a wrist-worn wearable and labeled sleep from polysomnography
subjects: 31 subjects in the release. Thirty-nine were recruited; eight were excluded
recordings: One in-lab night of Apple Watch motion and heart rate with PSG-derived stage labels per released subject, plus ambulatory step counts
modalities: Apple Watch acceleration, photoplethysmography heart rate, step counts, and PSG stage labels. Raw PSG waveforms are not in the release
sampling_rate: Not a fixed PSG rate. Acceleration and heart rate are timestamped watch samples
annotations: PSG stages coded 0 wake, 1 N1, 2 N2, 3 N3, 5 REM, timed in seconds from PSG start
clinical_text: No
license: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
research_use: Open download. Attribution required. The paper is Walch et al., Sleep 2019
paper: Walch, Huang, Forger, and Goldstein, Sleep 2019; zsz180
multi_expert: No
timed_events: Stage labels only. No EEG waveform to localize
cover_stage2: Useful for wearable staging. Cannot support EEG or PSG signal-level evidence grounding
notes: Exclusions included data-transmission failure, sleep apnea, and REM sleep behavior disorder, so the released cohort is not a sleep-disorder cohort. Paper DOI 10.1093/sleep/zsz180; dataset DOI is the PhysioNet DOI above.

name: Dreem Open Datasets (DOD-H and DOD-O)
subjects: Paper: 25 healthy (DOD-H) and 55 obstructive sleep apnea (DOD-O). Official code note: the Zenodo DOD-O archive contains 56 HDF5 files, one without a consensus annotation
recordings: One night per included record. DOD-H zip listing inspected on the Zenodo page contains 25 HDF5 records
modalities: Overnight PSG in HDF5. Official code examples reference EEG (C3-M2, F4-M1, F3-F4, F3-M2, F4-O2) and EOG. The complete montage was not exported from an HDF5 header in this pass
sampling_rate: Not stated as one official rate in the files inspected. The example pipeline resamples selected signals to 100 Hz
annotations: Five sleep technologists from different centers scored both cohorts, and a consensus hypnogram is the documented HDF5 label. Stage codes include unscored (-1), wake, N1, N2, N3, and REM. Whether every individual scorer vector is inside each 2025 HDF5 file was not byte-checked
clinical_text: No
license: Zenodo record 15900394 states MIT License
research_use: Direct Zenodo download. The record's rights field says MIT. Cite Guillot et al. 2020 as the dataset paper
paper: Guillot, Sauvet, During, and Thorey, IEEE TNSRE 2020
multi_expert: Yes in the study design: five scorers. Confirm that the downloaded files, not only the paper, contain the separate score vectors
timed_events: Sleep-stage epochs. Spindle, K-complex, and apnea-interval layers are not described in the Zenodo file summary
cover_stage2: Best open candidate for multi-scorer staging at moderate sample size, with a healthy versus OSA split. Verify the per-scorer arrays before designing the disagreement experiment
notes: Paper DOI commonly indexed as 10.1109/TNSRE.2020.3011181. To reproduce the paper, the code README says to exclude DOD-O record 5d8e93a5-d26a-436d-bc2c-e9527dc92cbf. Code license and data license are both reported as MIT, but they are separate objects.

name: Bitbrain Open Access Sleep (BOAS)
version: OpenNeuro ds005555; dataset_description.json on the GitHub mirror cites v1.1.3
subjects: 100 adults from the general population
recordings: 128 simultaneous full nights of clinical PSG and wearable EEG
modalities: Micromed PSG, including EEG and respiratory belts and thermistor as described in the dataset README, plus a Bitbrain forehead EEG headband with movement and photoplethysmography
sampling_rate: Accompanying code treats the EEG as 256 Hz and can downsample to 128 Hz. An EDF header was not opened in this pass
annotations: Three experts scored PSG by AASM rules and a consensus was derived. AI stage labels are also released. Code analyzes individual scorers, consensus, and AI labels; the event-file columns were not opened here
clinical_text: No. participants.tsv includes age, sex, and BMI
license: Data: CC0 in dataset_description.json on the OpenNeuro GitHub mirror. Code repository: CC BY-NC 4.0, which does not replace the data license
research_use: Direct OpenNeuro download. Manuscript was still described as forthcoming on the code README checked 2026-11-05
paper: Manuscript forthcoming according to the project README. Dataset citation requested by the maintainers uses the OpenNeuro DOI
multi_expert: Three experts are described. Confirm whether the public events contain three raw score tracks or only the consensus plus AI
timed_events: 30 s stage labels, including disconnection and artifact codes in the published README summary. Micro-event layers are not described
cover_stage2: Best open simultaneous PSG-versus-wearable set. Disagreement analysis depends on whether individual scorer tracks are actually in the events
notes: A DataCite record for v1.2.0 was seen in search and was not diffed against v1.1.3. Ethics approval is cited as Comité de Ética de la Investigación de la Comunidad Autónoma de Aragón, C.I. PI24/046. That approval governed collection; it is not an access gate.

name: DREAMS Databases
year: Zenodo record date 2005; recordings belong to the earlier DREAMS project
subjects: Subsets, not one cohort: 20 healthy whole nights, 27 patient whole nights, plus smaller excerpt sets
recordings: Subjects 20 whole-night PSGs; Patients 27; PLM 10 whole nights; Apnea 12 whole nights; Artifacts 20 excerpts of 15 min; Spindles 8 excerpts of 30 min; K-complexes 5 excerpts of 30 min; REMs 9 excerpts of 30 min
modalities: PSG acquired on a 32-channel Brainnet system and stored in EDF. Excerpt databases may contain only the central EEG or the relevant channel
sampling_rate: Not extracted from the EDF headers in this pass. See the PDF bundled in the Zenodo record
annotations: Whole-night subsets scored in both R&K and AASM stages. Spindles and K-complexes were marked independently by two experts. Artifacts, REMs, PLMs, and respiratory events have expert marks in their own subsets
clinical_text: No
license: Bundled Dreams License.txt matches Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 3.0: non-commercial, and no adaptations beyond technically necessary format changes
research_use: Direct download. Non-commercial. The no-derivatives clause is restrictive; this catalog does not decide whether model training is an adaptation. Read the license before training or redistributing derivatives
paper: Devuyst, Kerkhofs, and Dutoit, DREAMS project databases. Publication list is linked from the Zenodo description
multi_expert: Yes for spindle and K-complex excerpts (two experts). Whole-night stage files are not described as parallel multi-scorer copies
timed_events: Yes inside the relevant subset: spindles, K-complexes, REMs, PLMs, artifacts, and respiratory events
cover_stage2: Best open microstructure disagreement set, with a serious license constraint and a known spindle-score truncation
notes: The Zenodo description warns that expert 1 spindle marks were cut off after 1000 seconds, so spindle counts are not comparable. Excerpt databases are not whole-night context.

name: ISRUC-Sleep
version: Public site as reviewed 2026-11-05; no version number stated
subjects: 118 (100 + 8 + 10), from the official homepage structure
recordings: 126 (100 single nights, 16 from two sessions in 8 subjects, and 10 healthy single nights)
modalities: Full-night PSG: EEG, EOG, EMG, and additional physiological signals. The current homepage does not restate the electrode list
sampling_rate: Unknown on the pages reviewed. Secondary conversions report 200 Hz; that figure is not adopted here
annotations: Two human experts visually scored the PSG recordings. The homepage states this for the dataset as a whole
clinical_text: No narrative report. Subject metadata are part of the download description
license: No standard public license is posted. The download page says the dataset is publicly available for research purposes
research_use: Direct download links are presented, with a MEGA bandwidth caveat and an offer to contact the maintainers. Research purpose is stated; commercial use is not granted in a license text
paper: Khalighi, Sousa, Santos, and Nunes, Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine 2016;124:180-192
multi_expert: Yes. Two experts, as stated on the current official homepage and download page
timed_events: Sleep-stage annotations. A public event-interval layer was not verified on the pages reviewed
cover_stage2: Best larger two-expert open PSG candidate, plus a two-night subset. License is not a standard open license, and one official page currently contradicts another
notes: Homepage: group 1 is 100 subjects with one session; group 2 is 8 subjects with two sessions; group 3 is 10 healthy subjects. The download page instead calls cohort II healthy. Do not rely on the download-page diagnosis for cohort II until the maintainers reconcile it. The paper DOI is the journal article, not a data DOI.

name: MODA spindle annotations
version: Gold-standard release described on the OSF wiki
subjects: 180 MASS recordings used for spindle scoring. The annotation download does not include those PSGs
recordings: Annotation files for the 180-recording gold standard. Waveforms remain in MASS
modalities: Spindle marks referring to MASS EEG. No waveform in the open annotation release
sampling_rate: Not applicable to the annotation release. Source EEG is MASS, which is controlled
annotations: Crowdsourced and expert spindle marks, with a gold-standard set and confidence in later releases
clinical_text: No
license: OSF wiki presents the annotations as freely available. A single SPDX license was not copied from a license file in this pass
research_use: Annotations can be downloaded from OSF and GitHub. Using them with signals requires MASS access and local ethics approval
paper: Lacourse, Yetton, Mednick, and Warby, Scientific Data 2020;7:190
multi_expert: Yes for spindle perception, including non-expert and expert markers. This is not sleep-stage disagreement
timed_events: Spindle intervals only, and only if joined to MASS signals obtained separately
cover_stage2: Do not treat MODA as an open PSG. It becomes a pointer resource only after MASS waveforms are legally obtained
notes: The MODA_GC README states that MASS PSG access requires a project approved by the requester's ethics board and proof of that approval. One hundred eighty of 200 shared PSGs were used.

name: Sleep Heart Health Study
subjects: Same official page gives two figures: the header says 5,804 adults, and the about text says 6,441 enrolled in Visit 1. Do not collapse them
recordings: A second PSG was obtained in 3,295 participants. The exact current EDF count was not taken from the authenticated file tree
modalities: Overnight PSG at Visit 1 and Visit 2, plus covariate and cardiovascular-outcome tables
sampling_rate: Documented in the NSRR montage pages. Not re-copied here
annotations: Scored PSG events and summary variables after approval. Reliability notes exist for both visits
clinical_text: Forms, manuals, and coded outcomes. Not a public free-text PSG-report corpus
license: NSRR Data Access and Use Agreement after manual review. IRB review is preferred; a  forum reply says it is not a firm requirement for SHHS and an internal-review option exists
research_use: Not a direct download. Create an account, submit a request, and wait for approval. Commercial use must match the dataset agreement
paper: Quan et al., Sleep 1997;20:1077-1085; Zhang et al., JAMIA 2018;25:1351-1358
multi_expert: Not established as public parallel labels. Reliability documentation should be read after access
timed_events: Yes in the NSRR PSG annotation files after access. Not inspected in this pass
cover_stage2: Important controlled cohort for later generalization. It is outside the open-data experiments
notes: The page banner on 2026-11-05 said the repository is under review for possible modification under administration directives. Re-check access terms before applying. Header and about-text sample sizes disagree.

name: MESA Sleep
subjects: Parent MESA cohort 6,814. Sleep exam enrollment 2,237
recordings: Full overnight unattended PSG and 7-day wrist actigraphy for the sleep exam. Exact released file counts were not taken from the authenticated tree. A third-party reader documents 2,056 annotated PSGs; that number is not the official inventory
modalities: PSG, wrist actigraphy, sleep questionnaire, and MESA Sleep covariates
sampling_rate: See the NSRR montage page after access. Not re-copied here
annotations: Scored PSG and actigraphy after approval
clinical_text: Questionnaire and coded covariates, not PSG-report prose
license: NSRR Data Access and Use Agreement. The dataset page exposes Request Data Access
research_use: Manual request. Other MESA exams are a separate BioLINCC process
paper: Chen et al., Sleep 2015;38:877-888; Zhang et al., JAMIA 2018
multi_expert: Not described on the public about page
timed_events: PSG annotation files are part of the released tree after approval. Not inspected here
cover_stage2: Controlled multi-ethnic PSG plus actigraphy. Not an open substitute for BOAS or Sleep-Accel
notes: The same administration-review banner seen on SHHS was present. Do not cite 2,056 as the NSRR official count.

name: Montreal Archive of Sleep Studies
version: Cohort described by O'Reilly et al. 2014; Borealis deposits updated later
subjects: Subset example from the public Borealis descriptions: SS1 53 subjects, SS2 19 subjects. The full-cohort total was not re-summed from every subset page
recordings: Whole-night laboratory PSGs. SS2 staging uses 20 s pages under R&K; SS1 uses 30 s pages under AASM, according to the Borealis descriptions
modalities: EEG, EOG, EMG, ECG, and respiration in EDF+. Montage differs by subset
sampling_rate: Not copied from EDF headers. Access to those headers is restricted
annotations: Sleep stages travel with the biosignal request. Some subset annotations, including SS2 spindles and K-complexes, are public downloads on Borealis. Expert 2 spindles cover 15 of 19 SS2 subjects
clinical_text: No
license: Custom terms. Biosignals require a project description approved by the requester's ethics board and proof of that approval. Restricted descriptors also need hypothesis review
research_use: Not direct download for waveforms. Email mass.cnmtl@ssss.gouv.qc.ca or request through Borealis. Open-access descriptors and some annotation files are less restricted
paper: O'Reilly, Gosselin, Carrier, and Nielsen, Journal of Sleep Research 2014;23:628-635
multi_expert: SS2 spindle marks include a second expert for 15 subjects. Whole-night staging is not described as a general multi-scorer release
timed_events: Public annotation files include spindles and K-complexes for SS2. The corresponding EEG is Tier C
cover_stage2: High value after ethics approval, especially with MODA and SS2 microstructure. Not eligible for the open main tables
notes: The project calls itself open-access, but the access page explicitly says PSG biosignals will never be available for direct download. Follow the access page, not the adjective.

name: MrOS Sleep Study
subjects: Header says 2,911 men aged 65 or older. The about text says 3,135 were recruited to the sleep study. The dataset introduction says Visit 1 has 2,911 rows with successful PSG
recordings: Visit 2 table has 2,911 rows, of which 1,026 subjects had repeated sleep measures, per the dataset introduction
modalities: Unattended overnight PSG. The NSRR copy says actigraphy raw data and results are not included
sampling_rate: See the NSRR montage pages. Not re-copied here
annotations: PSG summaries and annotation files after approval
clinical_text: Coded forms and variables, not a report corpus
license: NSRR Data Access and Use Agreement. The files page shows Request Data Access
research_use: Manual request. Additional MrOS variables may require the San Francisco Coordinating Center
paper: NSRR MrOS documentation and Zhang et al., JAMIA 2018
doi: Unknown; the files page was checked for the request gate, and a dataset DOI was not transcribed
multi_expert: Not stated on the pages reviewed
timed_events: PSG annotation files after access. Not inspected
cover_stage2: Controlled older-male cohort. Not an open evidence-grounding set
notes: Keep 3,135 recruited, 2,911 successful Visit 1 PSGs, and 1,026 repeat sleep measures as separate numbers.

name: Cleveland Family Study
version: NSRR posting; Visit 5 PSG released first
subjects: 2,284 individuals from 361 families
recordings: Visit 5 included full overnight PSG. The page says earlier visits will be posted later. File counts were not taken from the authenticated tree
modalities: Overnight PSG and core phenotype tables
sampling_rate: Not re-copied
annotations: PSG scoring for the released visit after approval
clinical_text: Coded study data, not report prose
license: NSRR request. The dataset page states the CFS dataset is only available for non-commercial use
research_use: Manual approval plus a non-commercial restriction beyond the generic NSRR flow
paper: NSRR CFS about page; Zhang et al., JAMIA 2018
multi_expert: Not stated
timed_events: Not inspected
cover_stage2: Controlled family sleep-apnea cohort. Non-commercial terms are an additional constraint
notes: Do not assume every one of the 2,284 individuals has a downloadable PSG. The page limits the initial release to Visit 5.

name: Stanford Technology Analytics and Genomics in Sleep
version: NSRR, with Mayo Clinic PSGs removed in June 2023
subjects: 1,500 adult and adolescent patients evaluated for sleep disorders
recordings: Nocturnal PSGs from multiple sites. Exact current EDF count was not re-counted. Four duplicate EDF pairs are listed by NSRR
modalities: PSG (EEG, chin and leg EMG, nasal and oral breathing, chest movement, leg movement, position, ECG), Alliance Sleep Questionnaire, actigraphy counts. Facial scans and medical-record data are not on NSRR
sampling_rate: Not re-copied
annotations: Clinical PSG files and questionnaire variables after approval
clinical_text: Structured questionnaire and medication data. The page does not describe free-text PSG reports linked to waveforms
license: NSRR request and approval. The preamble says non-commercial and commercial use are both allowed
research_use: The phrase publicly available on the about page is explicitly conditioned on an approved NSRR request
paper: NSRR STAGES about page
multi_expert: Not stated
timed_events: Clinical PSG annotations are expected in the EDF release. Not inspected
cover_stage2: Controlled clinical PSG plus rich questionnaires. Adolescent participants mean the cohort is not adults-only. Not open
notes: NSRR removed Mayo Clinic PSGs in June 2023 because of conversion problems and listed duplicate EDF pairs that can share or split subject identifiers. Account for both before any experiment.

name: DREAMT
subjects: 100 participants with sleep apnea or otherwise abnormal sleep
recordings: In-lab sleep studies with smartwatch signals and PSG alignment. Per-subject night count was not separately stated beyond the 100-participant release
modalities: High-resolution smartwatch signals, PSG-aligned data, technician sleep-stage labels, and sleep-disorder metadata. Version 2.2.0 fixes accelerometer and PSG misalignment
sampling_rate: Described as high resolution. Exact rates were not copied from the restricted files
annotations: Expert sleep-technician stage labels and clinical sleep metadata
clinical_text: Clinical metadata related to sleep health and disorders. Not described as full PSG-report text
license: PhysioNet Restricted Health Data License 1.5.0 and the matching restricted data use agreement
research_use: Qualified requestors only. Research use, no redistribution of access, no re-identification. Not an ordinary PhysioNet open bucket
paper: Wang, Yang, Shetty, and Dunn, PhysioNet, 2026
